# The variable register

Every row in the tree, with the unit it publishes in, the range over which it
is declared valid, and the reason for each bound. A guard whose reason is not
written down gets deleted by the next person who finds it awkward, so the
reasons are part of the register rather than a comment in the code.

**250 rows** — 112 a person picked, 138 worked out. Two thirds of any design tree is
the first kind: cheaper than a computed node, and not free, because every margin
in the design is built out of them.


## `aero` — Aerodynamics and drag

### `aero_accommodation` — Energy accommodation coefficient

> How completely does an incoming molecule thermalise with the surface before leaving?

| | |
|---|---|
| symbol | `alpha` |
| type | `Ratio` |
| unit | - |
| kind | computed |
| owner | aero |
| evidence tier | B |
| relation | `alpha = K*n_O*T_inf/(1 + K*n_O*T_inf),  K = 7.5e-17` |
| source | `moe2005` |
| valid over | 0 … 1 - |

- **lower bound** — accommodation is a fraction and cannot be negative
- **upper bound** — full accommodation is one; above it the reflected molecules would carry away energy the surface does not have
- **reads** — `env_atomic_oxygen_density`, `env_exospheric_temperature`
- **read by** — `aero_drag_coefficient`
- **assumes** The surface is covered in adsorbed atomic oxygen and behaves as that coverage dictates — fails when a freshly cleaned or a fluorinated surface adsorbs far less, and its drag differs by tens of per cent from this
- **evidence** — none. Nothing outside this code has agreed with what it computes, so its validation credibility factor is zero, which governs the whole vector.

A design that assumes a fixed accommodation has a margin that moves when the Sun does.

### `aero_ao_fluence` — Atomic oxygen fluence

> How many oxygen atoms strike a forward-facing surface over the mission?

| | |
|---|---|
| symbol | `F_AO` |
| type | `Ratio` |
| unit | - |
| kind | computed |
| owner | mass |
| evidence tier | B |
| relation | `F = n_O*V*t` |
| source | `moe2005` |
| valid over | 0 … 100000000000000000000000000 - |

- **lower bound** — a fluence cannot be negative
- **upper bound** — above 1e26 atoms per square metre no known external material survives, so the design is not a design
- **reads** — `env_atomic_oxygen_density`, `orbit_velocity`, `orbit_mission_duration`
- **read by** — nothing yet. Every one of these is a leaf of the design, or an oversight.
- **contributes to** — kpi_service_lifetime
- **evidence** — none. Nothing outside this code has agreed with what it computes, so its validation credibility factor is zero, which governs the whole vector.

Polyimide erodes at about 3e-24 cm3 per incident atom, so 1e22 removes roughly 30 micrometres of it.

### `aero_appendage_area` — Appendage frontal area

> How much frontal area do the array, antennas and radiators add beyond the body?

| | |
|---|---|
| symbol | `A_app` |
| type | `Area` |
| unit | m^2 |
| kind | declared |
| owner | mass |
| evidence tier | A |
| relation | `A_app = 0.05` |
| source | `orbitt_case_c1` |
| declared value | **0.05** m^2 |
| confirmed by | A. Rai / 2026-09-01 |
| valid over | 0 … 5 m^2 |

- **lower bound** — an area cannot be negative
- **upper bound** — above 5 m2 of appendage the design is an array with a satellite attached, and the drag closure is decided by the array alone
- **read by** — `aero_frontal_area`

Separated from the body area because it is the term a power or thermal decision moves, and the tree has to show that coupling.

### `aero_ballistic_coefficient` — Ballistic coefficient

> How well does this vehicle resist the atmosphere, per unit of its own mass?

| | |
|---|---|
| symbol | `BC` |
| type | `Ratio` |
| unit | - |
| kind | computed |
| owner | aero |
| evidence tier | A |
| relation | `BC = m/(Cd*A)` |
| source | `vallado2013` |
| valid over | 5 … 500 - |

- **lower bound** — below 5 kg/m2 the vehicle is a sail, and nothing in this band closes
- **upper bound** — above 500 kg/m2 the vehicle is denser than any spacecraft ever flown
- **reads** — `mass_wet`, `aero_drag_coefficient`, `aero_frontal_area`
- **read by** — `orbit_decay_rate`, `orbit_lifetime_uncontrolled`
- **evidence** — none. Nothing outside this code has agreed with what it computes, so its validation credibility factor is zero, which governs the whole vector.

Higher is better here. A cubesat is around 50; a slender VLEO platform reaches 150, and that difference is worth tens of kilometres of altitude.

| owner | gnc |

| source | `orbitt_case_c1` |
| declared value | **0.15** m |
| confirmed by | A. Rai / 2026-09-01 |
| valid over | 0 … 2 m |

- **read by** — `aero_torque`, `gnc_solar_torque`

Positive means aft, which is the stable configuration. Arranging that is most of what passive aerostability in VLEO means.

### `aero_drag_coefficient` — Drag coefficient

> What is the drag coefficient of this body, at this speed ratio, with this surface?

| | |
|---|---|
| symbol | `Cd` |
| type | `Ratio` |
| unit | - |
| kind | computed |
| owner | aero |
| evidence tier | A |
| relation | `Cd = P/sqrt(pi) + gamma*Q*Z + (gamma/2)*vr*(gamma*sqrt(pi)*Z + P)` |
| source | `doornbos2011` |
| valid over | 1.5 … 5 - |

- **lower bound** — no free-molecular body has a drag coefficient below 1.5; a lower value means the speed ratio or the accommodation is wrong
- **upper bound** — above 5.0 the geometry is not the slender body this model assumes
- **reads** — `aero_speed_ratio`, `aero_body_length`, `aero_body_diameter`, `aero_accommodation`, `env_wall_temperature`, `orbit_velocity`, `env_mean_molar_mass`, `env_knudsen`
- **read by** — `aero_ballistic_coefficient`, `aero_drag_force`
- **assumes** Free-molecular flow — a molecule leaving the surface never returns and never strikes an incoming one — fails when below Kn = 10, which is roughly 150 km for this body; the Knudsen number is an input so that the guard on it is visible here
- **evidence** 250 km cylinder, moderate activity — expect 2.85807 ± 0.001 relative, from `matlab_legacy` (independent-tool)

Treating this as a constant 2.2 is the single largest avoidable error in a VLEO drag estimate, and it is what most concept studies do.

### `aero_drag_force` — Drag force

### `aero_speed_ratio` — Molecular speed ratio

> How hyperthermal is the flow — does the gas arrive as a beam or as a cloud?

| | |
|---|---|
| symbol | `s` |
| type | `Ratio` |
| unit | - |
| kind | computed |
| owner | aero |
| evidence tier | A |
| relation | `s = V/sqrt(2*R*T/M)` |
| source | `sentman1961` |
| valid over | 1 … 30 - |

- **lower bound** — below a speed ratio of one the flow is thermal rather than hyperthermal, and Sentman's relations lose their meaning
- **upper bound** — above 30 the exponential terms underflow and the relations are numerically dead
- **reads** — `orbit_velocity`, `env_local_temperature`, `env_mean_molar_mass`
- **read by** — `aero_drag_coefficient`
- **evidence** 250 km, moderate activity — expect 8.6435 ± 0.005 relative, from `sentman1961` (independent-derivation)

In VLEO this dominates gravity gradient and solar pressure by one to three orders of magnitude, which is why a control design carried over from a higher orbit is undersized here.

- **evidence** moderate activity — expect 949.6 ± 0.002 relative, from `jacchia1971` (published-source)
- **evidence** solar maximum, storm — expect 1417.9 ± 0.002 relative, from `jacchia1971` (published-source)

- **read by** — `gnc_magnetic_torque`, `gnc_magnetorquer_dipole`
- **assumes** Centred dipole, no higher-order terms — fails when the South Atlantic Anomaly departs from a dipole by up to 30%; a magnetorquer sized on this alone is undersized there
- **evidence** — none. Nothing outside this code has agreed with what it computes, so its validation credibility factor is zero, which governs the whole vector.

### `env_mass_density` — Atmospheric mass density

> How much air is there at the flight altitude, in kilograms per cubic metre?

| | |
|---|---|
| symbol | `rho` |
| type | `MassDensity` |
| unit | kg/m^3 |
| kind | computed |
| owner | environment |
| evidence tier | B |
| relation | `rho = SUM_i n_i(z)*m_i,  n_i(z) = n_i(z0)*(T0/T)^(1+alpha_i)*exp(-INT M_i*g/(R*T) dz)` |
| source | `jacchia1971` |
| valid over | 0.000000000000001 … 0.000001 kg/m^3 |

- **lower bound** — below 1e-15 kg/m3 the free-molecular relations downstream stop producing a meaningful drag
- **upper bound** — above 1e-6 kg/m3 the flow is no longer free-molecular and every aerodynamic node in this tree is outside its envelope
- **reads** — `orbit_altitude`, `env_exospheric_temperature`
- **read by** — `aero_dynamic_pressure`, `orbit_decay_rate`, `prop_collected_flow`, `prop_incident_flux`, `thm_aero_heating`
- **contributes to** — kpi_service_lifetime
- **assumes** Diffusive equilibrium above 120 km, five species — fails when below about 100 km turbulent mixing dominates and species do not separate; the model is not valid there
- **assumes** No diurnal, seasonal or longitudinal variation — fails when the real density at a fixed altitude varies by a factor of two around the orbit; this returns the daily mean
- **evidence** 250 km, moderate activity — expect 0.00000000006631 ± 0.005 relative, from `matlab_legacy` (independent-tool)
- **evidence** 400 km, moderate activity — expect 0.000000000002907 ± 0.005 relative, from `matlab_legacy` (independent-tool)
- **evidence** 200 km, solar minimum — expect 0.0000000001679 ± 0.005 relative, from `matlab_legacy` (independent-tool)

## `orbit` — Orbit geometry

### `orbit_altitude` — Orbit altitude

> At what altitude does the constellation fly? This is the one parameter the whole architecture is shaped around.

| | |
|---|---|
| symbol | `h` |
| type | `Length` |
| unit | km |
| kind | declared |
| owner | systems |
| evidence tier | A |
| relation | `h = 250` |
| source | `orbitt_case_c1` |
| declared value | **250** km |
| confirmed by | A. Rai / 2026-09-01 |
| valid over | 150 … 450 km |

- **lower bound** — below 150 km the flow stops being free-molecular for a body of this size and every aerodynamic node in the tree is outside its envelope
- **upper bound** — above 450 km there is not enough air for the air-breathing concept to be the reason for the design
- **read by** — `env_atomic_oxygen_density`, `env_local_temperature`, `env_mass_density`, `env_mean_molar_mass`, `env_number_density`, `env_scale_height`, `orbit_deorbit_delta_v`, `orbit_lifetime_uncontrolled`, `orbit_radius`, `pay_gsd_detector`, `pay_gsd_diffraction`
- **contributes to** — kpi_revisit, kpi_gsd, kpi_service_lifetime

Move this one value and 54 other nodes become stale. That is the requirement the tool exists to satisfy.

Moving this reaches 3 nodes. Moving the altitude reaches 54. The difference is the answer to how much of the design a change just invalidated.

### `orbit_eclipse_fraction` — Eclipse fraction of the orbit

- **read by** — nothing yet. Every one of these is a leaf of the design, or an oversight.

### `orbit_velocity` — Circular orbital speed

> How fast is the spacecraft moving through the atmosphere?

| | |
|---|---|
| symbol | `V` |
| type | `Velocity` |
| unit | m/s |
| kind | computed |
| owner | systems |
| evidence tier | A |
| relation | `V = sqrt(mu/r)` |
| source | `vallado2013` |
| valid over | 7000 … 8200 m/s |

- **lower bound** — below 7 km/s corresponds to an orbit above 1000 km, outside this tool's band

- **reads** — `orbit_radius`

- **assumes** Two-body, circular — fails when at e = 0.05 the speed varies by 5% around the orbit and a drag figure computed at the mean underestimates the perigee pass
- **evidence** 250 km circular — expect 7754.84549737 ± 0.000000001 relative, from `vallado2013` (independent-derivation)
- **evidence** 400 km circular — expect 7668.55817541 ± 0.000000001 relative, from `vallado2013` (independent-derivation)

### `prop_capture_efficiency` — Intake collection efficiency

> What fraction of the flow entering the mouth actually reaches the thruster?

| | |
|---|---|
| symbol | `eta_c` |
| type | `Ratio` |
| unit | - |
| kind | computed |
| owner | propulsion |
| evidence tier | B |
| relation | `eta_c = A_out*eta_geo/(A_out + beta*A_in)` |
| source | `romano2021` |
| valid over | 0 … 1 - |

- **lower bound** — a collection efficiency cannot be negative
- **upper bound** — an intake cannot deliver more than enters its mouth
- **reads** — `prop_intake_area`, `prop_throat_area`, `prop_eta_geo`, `prop_beta_backflow`, `env_chamber_temperature`, `env_mean_molar_mass`, `env_number_density`, `orbit_velocity`
- **read by** — `prop_collected_flow`
- **contributes to** — kpi_thrust_margin
- **assumes** Free-molecular flow throughout the duct and the chamber — fails when if the chamber compresses far enough to become collisional the balance is no longer a simple flux balance, which happens above a compression ratio of roughly 1e4
- **assumes** The chamber gas is fully thermalised at the chamber temperature — fails when a short duct passes part of the beam straight through, which raises the delivered flow above this and is not modelled
- **evidence** IRS-class baseline intake — expect 0.40909 ± 0.0001 relative, from `romano2021` (independent-derivation)

Read the relation slowly: the collection efficiency does not depend on the flight speed at all, only on geometry. Speed buys compression, not capture. A design trying to raise capture by flying faster is optimising the wrong term.
